summary: Thoroughly tested Gaia Hermes backend (SSE streaming, tool calls, artifacts, uploads, edit/retry) and Gaia Desktop UI (conversation flow, artifact card+canvas, tool card, retry/edit, threads, model-agnosticism). Backend: 12/12 pytest tests pass. Frontend: all critical flows work end-to-end against the live preview URL — streaming replies render, tool card renders result 842493, artifact card renders and canvas opens with syntax-highlighted code and closes cleanly, retry regenerates, edit-and-resend updates the user turn, thread list creates/switches/deletes, and NO provider/model names ('gpt', 'openai', 'claude', 'gemini', 'model version', etc.) are present anywhere in the visible UI text after multiple turns.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~510 lines — still readable but approaching the point where splitting (models, storage, tools, streaming) into modules would help maintainability.

download_file (/api/files/{path}) is publicly readable by anyone who knows the storage_path (UUID-based, so unguessable, but there is no auth guard — acceptable for the no-auth MVP but worth flagging).

In stream_message, the truncation predicate uses created_at >= target.created_at as a string comparison; safe because ISO-8601 UTC strings sort lexicographically, but consider indexing (conversation_id, created_at) in Mongo for large histories.
put_object / get_object are sync `requests` calls made from inside async endpoints (blocks the event loop). Fine for a dev-stub but should become async (httpx) if concurrency matters.
No pagination on GET /api/hermes/conversations (hard limit 200) — fine for MVP; document the cap.
Frontend model-agnosticism verified: after multiple prompts including tool calls, no provider/model tokens appear in body text.
seed_data_creation: Each test creates a fresh conversation and deletes it in teardown; upload test uses an in-memory 32x32 PNG generated by PIL. No permanent seed data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py exports BASE_URL from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL — set that env var before running pytest. pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope. Streaming endpoint is a POST that returns text/event-stream; use requests.iter_lines with stream=True. SSE events are JSON payloads on lines beginning with 'data: '. Tool events come as {type:'tool', status:'running'|'done', name, args, result}. Artifact markers are the fullwidth brackets 【artifact ...】 ... 【/artifact】 — must match those exact characters.
